predecessors.name: North Yemen
predecessors.text: the Yemen Arab Republic (North Yemen), proclaimed in 1962

predecessors.name: People's Democratic Republic of Yemen
predecessors.text: the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen (South Yemen), independent in 1967

ledger.x: 1990: North and South Yemen unite as the Republic of Yemen.
1990: the Yemen Arab Republic (North Yemen) enters the union; its dossier ends the same day.
1990: South Yemen enters the union; its dossier ends the same day.
2014: the Houthis seize Sanaa and the civil war begins.
2015: the government flees Sanaa for Aden.
2018: the Southern Transitional Council seizes Aden.

wars.name: 1994 civil war in Yemen
wars.outcome: The page says only that an accord between northern and southern leaders signed in Amman on 20 February 1994 'could not stop the civil war'; it is silent on the secession of the south, the winner and the fall of Aden.

wars.name: Houthi insurgency in Yemen
wars.outcome: 'The Houthi insurgency in Yemen began in June 2004', escalating in September 2014 when the Houthis swept into the capital and the civil war began.

wars.name: Saudi-led intervention in Yemen
wars.outcome: 'On 26 March 2015, Saudi Arabia announced Operation Decisive Storm', the start of the airstrikes; no change of frontier is recorded by the pages opened.

certainty.note: No border treaty is recorded on the Yemen page before the summer 2000 Saudi treaty; the Oman frontier (the page is silent on a 1992 agreement) and the Hanish Islands dispute with Eritrea (page silent) were not checked.
'Yemen and Saudi Arabia signed an International Border Treaty' in summer 2000.
